free_tier.stated: the software is free and self-hosted; the cost is a VPS and whatever upstream accounts it mounts

per_object_cap.stated: no cap of its own; the cap is the mounted upstream's

retention.stated: as long as the operator keeps the process and the upstream alive

egress.terms: unmetered by the software; the egress is whatever the upstream provider and any CDN in front charge

tooling: a single Go binary; REST under /api/*, WebDAV at /dav, an S3-compatible gateway, FTP and SFTP; the rclone alist backend works against it
chaining: the bridge layer of the whole topic: mount a pooled tenant or a pan account, serve it over REST and WebDAV, put a CDN in front

limits.value: the write gate is CanWriteContent (bit 3) OR a per-path meta override, evaluated in server/middlewares/fsup.go

identity_cost.detail: the operator installs it; a reader needs no account on the bridge itself

reliability_note: A community fork of AList, created in June 2025 after the AList project was sold and its ownership, docs and community were rewritten. The fork is the maintained one; AList v3 builds still run on many public instances and still work.

evidence.proved: the repository describes itself as 'A new AList Fork to Anti Trust Crisis', 25,183 stars, last push 2026-10-21
the write gate is: if !user.CanWriteContent() && !common.CanWriteContentBypassUserPerms(parentMeta, parentPath) then deny, then a second check common.CanWrite(user, parentMeta, parentPath)

the fs/list response carries Write: common.CanWrite(user, meta, reqPath) and WriteContentBypass: common.CanWriteContentBypassUserPerms(meta, reqPath); these are two different predicates and only the second mirrors the upload gate
the permission bitmask is documented in the struct comment: bit 3 is mkdir and upload, bit 8 is WebDAV read, bit 9 is WebDAV write
the AList project was reported sold in June 2025 and OpenList was created as a replacement that removes the original developer's private API links

notes: The one piece of this topic the client can own outright. The source is explicit that fs/list's write field is CanWrite, a per-user exclusion-list negation, while the upload gate is CanWriteContent(bit 3) OR a per-path meta; that distinction is why a host can report write:true and refuse every PUT, and why the one writable instance in the population reports write_content_bypass:true and permission 256 with no bit 3.

extras.aggregator_note: This record is the single home for both spellings of the aggregator, so the name the completeness audit called unindexed resolves here. the first appears in no index and is carried as an alias so a future pass searching for it finds this record.

binding_note: The bridge itself is not the constraint; what it can do is entirely set by which upstream it mounts and whether that upstream grants a write.
